s0004.literal: The Founder, Emperor Wu, had the tabooed name Baxian, the style name Xingguo, and the childhood name Fasheng. He was a native of Xiaruo Lane, Changcheng, Wuxing, and a descendant of Chen Shi, Magistrate of Taqiu in Han.
s0004.idiomatic: The Founder, Emperor Wu, whose personal name was tabooed as Baxian, styled himself Xingguo and was known in youth as Fasheng. He came from Xiaruo Lane in Changcheng, Wuxing, and traced his line to Chen Shi, magistrate of Taqiu in Han times.

s0005.literal: For generations the clan dwelt in Yingchuan.
s0005.idiomatic: For generations the family had lived in Yingchuan.

s0006.literal: Shi's great-great-grandson Zhun was Grand Commandant of Jin.
s0006.idiomatic: Chen Shi's great-great-grandson Zhun rose to be Grand Commandant of Jin.

s0007.literal: Zhun begat Kuang; Kuang begat Da. In the Yongjia era they migrated south. Da became an aide to the Chancellor, served successively as Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent, went out as Magistrate of Changcheng, delighted in its mountains and waters, and settled his household there.
s0007.idiomatic: Zhun's son was Kuang, and Kuang's son was Da. When the Yongjia turmoil drove the clan south, Da served as a chancellor's aide and then as attendant to the crown prince before being posted as magistrate of Changcheng. Charmed by the landscape, he made his home there.

s0008.literal: He once told those close to him: "The mountains and rivers of this place are splendid; a king will surely rise here. Two hundred years hence, my descendants will surely be granted this destiny.
s0008.idiomatic: He once told his intimates, "These mountains and streams are magnificent—a king will rise here. Two hundred years from now, my descendants will share in that fortune.

s0009.literal: " Da begat Kang, who again served as an aide to the Chancellor. In the Xianhe era the native register was discontinued, and henceforth they were accounted people of Changcheng.
s0009.idiomatic: " Da's son was Kang, who again served as a chancellor's aide. After the household register was broken off in the Xianhe era, the line was reckoned as Changcheng people.

s0010.literal: Kang begat Ying, Administrator of Xuyi; Ying begat Gongbi, Gentleman Attendant at the Masters of Writing; Gongbi begat Ding, Colonel of Foot Soldiers; Ding begat Gao, Attendant Gentleman-Companion in Ordinary; Gao begat Yong, Magistrate of Huai'an; Yong begat Meng, Administrator of Ancheng; Meng begat Daoju, Chamberlain for Ceremonials; Daoju begat the Founder's father Wenzan.
s0010.idiomatic: Kang's son Ying became administrator of Xuyi. Ying's son Gongbi served as a gentleman attendant in the Masters of Writing. Gongbi's son Ding was colonel of foot soldiers. Ding's son Gao was an attendant gentleman-companion in ordinary. Gao's son Yong was magistrate of Huai'an. Yong's son Meng was administrator of Ancheng. Meng's son Daoju was chamberlain for ceremonials. Daoju's son was the Founder's father, Wenzan.

s0011.literal: The Founder was born in the guiwei year, the second year of Tianjian of Liang.
s0011.idiomatic: The Founder was born in 503 CE, the guiwei year of Emperor Wu of Liang's Tianjian reign.

s0012.literal: In youth he was unconstrained and ambitious, and did not manage the household estate.
s0012.idiomatic: As a young man he was free-spirited and ambitious, with no taste for managing the family livelihood.

s0013.literal: Once grown, he read books of war, mastered many martial arts, was clear-sighted and decisive, and was admired by his contemporaries.
s0013.idiomatic: When he came of age he studied military writings and became skilled in many arms. Clear-minded, resolute, and decisive, he won the respect of all around him.

s0014.literal: His height was seven feet five inches; he had a sun-horn and dragon countenance, and his hands hung past his knees.
s0014.idiomatic: He stood seven feet five inches tall, with the sun-horn and dragon-countenance of imperial portent; when he stood at ease, his hands reached below his knees.

s0015.literal: Once, traveling in Yixing, he lodged with the Xu family. That night he dreamed the sky opened several zhang, and four men in vermilion robes came bearing the sun, bidding the Founder open his mouth to receive it. When he awoke, his belly was still warm; the Founder alone kept this to himself.
s0015.idiomatic: Once, while traveling in Yixing, he stayed with the Xu household. In the night he dreamed that the heavens split open for several yards and four men in crimson robes bore the sun to him, commanding him to open his mouth and take it in. When he woke, his belly was still warm. The Founder told no one and bore the omen in silence.

s0016.literal: In the early Datong era, Marquis of Xinyu Xiao Mo was Administrator of Wuxing.[1] He thought highly of the Founder and once fixed his gaze on him, telling his staff: "This man will go far.
s0016.idiomatic: Early in the Datong era, Xiao Mo, Marquis of Xinyu, served as administrator of Wuxing.[1] He held the Founder in high regard and once studied him closely before telling his aides, "This man is destined for great things.

s0017.literal: " When Mo became Inspector of Guangzhou, the Founder served as Middle Straight Troops Staff Officer and accompanied the headquarters to its post.
s0017.idiomatic: " When Mo was appointed inspector of Guangzhou, the Founder became a staff officer in the middle straight troops and went with the headquarters to take up the post.

s0018.literal: Mo ordered the Founder to gather gentlemen and horses until his force reached a thousand men, and then appointed him to oversee Songlong Commandery.
s0018.idiomatic: Mo had the Founder recruit men and horses until he had assembled a force of a thousand, then put him in charge of Songlong commandery.

s0019.literal: Within his jurisdiction the two counties of Anhua would not submit; the Founder attacked and pacified them.
s0019.idiomatic: The two counties of Anhua within his jurisdiction refused to submit; the Founder campaigned against them and brought them to order.

s0020.literal: Soon afterward he was made Supervisor of the West River Defense Command and Administrator of Gaoyao.
s0020.idiomatic: He was soon appointed supervisor of the West River defense command and administrator of Gaoyao.

s0021.literal: Earlier, Marquis of Wulin Xiao Zi had been Inspector of Jiaozhou. Through harsh exactions he lost the hearts of the people. The native leader Li Ben joined with magnates of several commanderies and rose in rebellion at the same time. The court sent Sun Tong, Inspector of Gaozhou, and Lu Zixiong, Inspector of Xinzhou, with troops to attack him. Tong and the others did not advance in time and were all executed at Guangzhou.
s0021.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiao Zi, Marquis of Wulin, had served as inspector of Jiaozhou. His grinding exactions cost him the people's loyalty. The local leader Li Ben rallied powerful men across several provinces in simultaneous revolt. The court dispatched Sun Tong of Gaozhou and Lu Zixiong of Xinzhou with armies against him, but they failed to advance promptly and were all put to death at Guangzhou.

s0022.literal: Zixiong's nephew's son Lue, together with Tong's sons and nephews and their commanders Du Tianhe and Du Sengming, all raised troops, seized the South River Defense Commander Shen Yan, and advanced to raid Guangzhou, attacking day and night until the province was shaken with fear.
s0022.idiomatic: Lu Zixiong's grandnephew Lue, together with Sun Tong's sons and nephews and their commanders Du Tianhe and Du Sengming, took up arms, seized the South River defense commander Shen Yan, and marched on Guangzhou in a bitter day-and-night assault that threw the province into terror.

s0023.literal: The Founder led three thousand picked troops, wrapped armor for forced marches, and went to the rescue. He fought repeatedly and won again and again. Tianhe was struck by a stray arrow and died; the rebel army broke in great rout, and Sengming then surrendered.
s0023.idiomatic: The Founder led three thousand elite troops, marching day and night in full armor to relieve the city. Battle after battle went his way. Tianhe took an arrow and died; the rebel host collapsed in rout, and Sengming surrendered.

s0024.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang marveled greatly and appointed him General of the Direct Gate, enfeoffed him as Viscount of Xin'an with a fief of three hundred households, and moreover sent painters to portray the Founder's features for his own viewing.
s0024.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang was deeply impressed. He made the Founder a general of the direct gate, enfeoffed him as Viscount of Xin'an with three hundred households, and even sent artists to paint his likeness so that the emperor might study it.

s0026.literal: The next year the Founder escorted the coffin back to the capital. At Dayu Ridge an edict arrived appointing him Vice Inspector of Jiaozhou and concurrent Administrator of Wuping, to campaign south with the Inspector Yang Yang.
s0026.idiomatic: The following year the Founder escorted the coffin homeward. At Dayu Ridge an imperial order arrived naming him vice inspector of Jiaozhou and concurrent administrator of Wuping, to march south with Inspector Yang Yang against the rebels.

s0027.literal: The Founder further recruited the brave; his weapons and equipment were keen.
s0027.idiomatic: The Founder recruited more bold fighters, and his arms and gear were of the finest.

s0028.literal: Yang said with pleasure: "The one who can defeat the bandits will surely be Chen the Staff Officer.
s0028.idiomatic: Yang said with delight, "The man who can crush these rebels will surely be Staff Officer Chen.

s0029.literal: " He entrusted him with overall strategy.
s0029.idiomatic: " He entrusted him with overall strategy.

s0030.literal: The Founder set out from Panyu with the army.
s0030.idiomatic: The Founder marched out of Panyu at the head of the army.

s0031.literal: At that time Xiao Bo was Inspector of Dingzhou. They met on the West River. Bo knew the soldiers feared a distant campaign and secretly bribed and tempted them, then spun false tales to Yang.
s0031.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Bo was inspector of Dingzhou. The two forces met on the West River. Bo knew the men dreaded service far from home; he secretly bought them off and fed Yang deceitful reports.

s0032.literal: Yang gathered the generals to ask their plans. The Founder replied: "Jiaozhi has rebelled and changed allegiance,[2] the fault lying with the imperial clan, which has allowed usurpation to spread across several provinces for many years.
s0032.idiomatic: Yang assembled his commanders to ask their counsel. The Founder answered, "Jiaozhi has turned rebel,[2] and the blame rests with the imperial house, which let usurpation fester across several provinces for years on end.

s0033.literal: Dingzhou again wishes to seize present profit and ignores the larger plan.
s0033.idiomatic: Now Dingzhou seeks only immediate gain and ignores the larger design.

s0034.literal: Your Grace bears the mandate to punish crime; I therefore owe you life and death. How can one fear the imperial clan and treat the state's laws lightly?
s0034.idiomatic: You bear the court's commission to punish wrongdoing; I owe you my life in this cause. How can we shrink before kinsmen of the throne and slight the laws of the realm?

s0035.literal: If we now discourage the troops, why need we go to Jiaozhou to punish bandits? The army bent on justice would turn its aim elsewhere.
s0035.idiomatic: If we now break the army's spirit, why march to Jiaozhou at all? A punitive host turned aside would strike somewhere else entirely.

s0036.literal: " Thereupon he marshaled the troops and advanced with drums beating.
s0036.idiomatic: " With that he drew up the army and advanced to the roll of drums.

s0037.literal: In the sixth month of the eleventh year the army reached Jiaozhou. Ben had several tens of thousands of men and built stockaded walls at the mouth of the Suli River to resist the government forces.
s0037.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eleventh year the army reached Jiaozhou. Li Ben had tens of thousands of men and threw up walled camps at the mouth of the Suli River to block the imperial forces.

s0038.literal: Yang pushed the Founder forward as vanguard; wherever he turned, defenses crumbled. Ben fled to Dianzhe Lake,[3] and on the border of Qu Liao he built a fortress and constructed many ships that filled the lake. The army feared this and halted at the lake mouth, not daring to advance.
s0038.idiomatic: Yang put the Founder in the van; nothing stood before him. Ben retreated to Dianzhe Lake,[3] and on the Qu Liao frontier he raised a stronghold and built a great fleet that choked the waters. The army hesitated at the lake mouth and dared not go forward.

s0039.literal: The Founder told the generals: "Our force is worn, officers and men are weary, and we have faced each other for a year—this is no good plan.
s0039.idiomatic: The Founder told his commanders, "Our troops are spent and the men exhausted; we have been locked here for a year. That is no strategy.

s0040.literal: Moreover we are a lone army without reinforcements, deep in the enemy's heartland. If one battle fails, can we hope to survive?
s0040.idiomatic: We are an isolated force without relief, deep in the enemy's core. Lose one battle and who expects to live?

s0041.literal: Now, relying on their repeated flight, men's hearts are not yet firm; the barbarians are a mob easily shattered. We should all stake our lives together and resolve to take them. To halt without cause is to let the moment slip away.
s0041.idiomatic: They have fled again and again; their morale is still unsteady. These tribal levies are a rabble that can be broken. We should all go forward ready to die and strike with everything we have. To linger here without reason is to lose the hour.

s0042.literal: " The generals were all silent; none answered.
s0042.idiomatic: " The commanders sat in silence; not one spoke up.

s0043.literal: That night the river water rose seven zhang in a sudden flood and poured into the lake in a swift, raging torrent.
s0043.idiomatic: That night the river surged seven zhang in a sudden flood and poured into the lake in a roaring torrent.

s0044.literal: The Founder led his troops, riding the current to advance first. The army raised a great clamor and pressed forward together. The rebel army broke in great rout. Ben fled into a Qu Liao cave; the Qu Liao beheaded Ben and sent his head to the capital.
s0044.idiomatic: The Founder led his men onto the flood and went first. The army thundered forward together. The rebels collapsed in rout. Ben fled into a Qu Liao cave; the Qu Liao killed him and sent his head to the capital.

s0045.literal: That year was the first year of Taiqing.
s0045.idiomatic: That year was the first year of the Taiqing era.

s0047.literal: Ben's elder brother Tianbao fled into Jiuzhen. With the bandit chief Li Shaolong he gathered twenty thousand remnant troops, killed Chen Wenzie, Inspector of Dezhou, and advanced to besiege Aizhou. The Founder again led troops and pacified them.
s0047.idiomatic: Ben's elder brother Tianbao escaped into Jiuzhen. With the bandit leader Li Shaolong he rallied twenty thousand survivors, killed Chen Wenzie, inspector of Dezhou, and marched to besiege Aizhou. The Founder led his army out once more and put them down.

s0048.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance, West River Defense Commander, Administrator of Gaoyao, and Supervisor of Military Affairs in seven commanderies.
s0048.idiomatic: He was made general who pacifies the distance, commander of the West River defense, administrator of Gaoyao, and supervisor of military affairs across seven commanderies.

s0049.literal: In the winter of the second year Hou Jing raided the capital. The Founder was about to lead troops to the rescue when Yuan Jingzhong, Inspector of Guangzhou, secretly harbored other designs and plotted against him.
s0049.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year Hou Jing struck at the capital. The Founder was preparing to march to the relief when Yuan Jingzhong, inspector of Guangzhou, secretly nursed other ambitions and plotted his downfall.

s0050.literal: The Founder learned of the plot. With Wang Huaiming, Inspector of Chengzhou, Yin Waichen, Gentleman Attendant of the Mobile Secretariat, and others he held secret counsel and ordered the guards to stand ready.
s0050.idiomatic: The Founder learned of the plot. With Wang Huaiming, inspector of Chengzhou, Yin Waichen of the mobile secretariat, and others he met in secret council and ordered the guards to stand to arms.

s0051.literal: In the seventh month of the third year he gathered righteous troops at Nanhai and sent a rapid proclamation to attack Jingzhong.
s0051.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year he mustered loyal troops at Nanhai and issued a swift manifesto to move against Jingzhong.

s0052.literal: Jingzhong was driven to extremity and hanged himself beneath the gate-tower. The Founder welcomed Xiao Bo to secure Guangzhou.
s0052.idiomatic: Jingzhong was cornered and hanged himself under the gate-tower. The Founder welcomed Xiao Bo to take charge of Guangzhou.

s0053.literal: At that time Ouyang Yong, Interior Minister of Linhe, was overseeing Hengzhou. Lan Yu and Lan Jingli incited more than ten commanderies including Shixing to raise troops together and attack Yong. Yong asked Bo for aid.
s0053.idiomatic: At that time Ouyang Yong, interior minister of Linhe, held Hengzhou. Lan Yu and Lan Jingli stirred Shixing and nine other commanderies to rise together against him. Yong appealed to Bo for help.

s0054.literal: Bo ordered the Founder to lead troops to rescue him, captured Yu and the others completely, and then put the Founder in charge of Shixing Commandery.
s0054.idiomatic: Bo ordered the Founder to march to his relief. He captured Yu and his fellows entirely and then made the Founder overseer of Shixing commandery.

s0055.literal: In the eleventh month the Founder sent Du Sengming and Hu Ying with two thousand men to encamp on the ridge, lavished gifts to win over the magnates of Shixing in a joint righteous rising, and Hou Andu, Zhang Si, and others led more than a thousand men to join him.
s0055.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent Du Sengming and Hu Ying with two thousand men to camp on the ridge, showered favors on the Shixing magnates to win them to a joint uprising, and Hou Andu, Zhang Si, and others brought more than a thousand followers to his banner.

s0056.literal: When Bo heard of this he sent Zhong Xiuyue to advise the Founder: "Hou Jing is fierce and heroic, unmatched under heaven. Earlier relief armies of a hundred thousand with elite troops and horses did not dare meet his edge, and the Jie bandit had his way. With your paltry force, where will you go?
s0056.idiomatic: When Bo heard of it he sent Zhong Xiuyue to warn the Founder: "Hou Jing is a savage champion, unmatched in the realm. Relief armies of a hundred thousand with the finest horses and arms would not face his spearhead, and the Jie rebel had his way. With your meager host, where can you go?

s0057.literal: I hear that north of the ridge the princes are all seething; Hedong and Guiyang have been slaughtered in turn; Shaoling and Kaijian are soon to take up arms against each other. Li Qianshi has thrown in his lot with Dangyang and even seized horses and armor. In your exposed position, how can you rush blindly into such danger?
s0057.idiomatic: They say the lords north of the mountains are all in uproar; Hedong and Guiyang have been put to the sword one after another; Shaoling and Kaijian are on the verge of civil war. Li Qianshi has sheltered himself in Dangyang and even seized horses and arms. With your position so exposed, how can you throw yourself blindly into such peril?

s0058.literal: You would do better to halt for now at Shixing, project your strength from afar, hold fast to this Mount Tai, and seek your own good fortune.
s0058.idiomatic: Better to hold at Shixing for now, raise your banners from afar, cling to this secure base, and look to your own survival.

s0059.literal: " The Founder wept and told Xiuyue: "I am by nature mediocre and empty, yet the state raised and made me.
s0059.idiomatic: " The Founder wept and said to Xiuyue, "I am a humble, worthless man whom the state raised and shaped.

s0060.literal: When I heard that Hou Jing had crossed the Yangtze I wished at once to go to the rescue, but Yuan and Lan blocked my path midway.
s0060.idiomatic: When I heard Hou Jing had crossed the Yangtze I wanted to rush to the rescue at once, but Yuan and Lan cut me off on the road.

s0061.literal: Now the capital has fallen and the sovereign suffers dust and hardship. When the ruler is shamed the minister must die—who dares spare his life!
s0061.idiomatic: Now the capital is lost and the emperor wanders in hardship. When the sovereign is disgraced the servant must die—who would cling to his life!

s0062.literal: Your lordship by lineage is an imperial branch; your burden is a great province. You cannot drive the spearhead ten thousand li and wipe away this grievous wrong. To send even one army would still be better than nothing—yet you issue words of retreat that make one sigh.
s0062.idiomatic: You are of the imperial blood and bear a great province on your shoulders. You cannot drive the spear ten thousand li to wash away this shame. To send even one army would still be something—yet you speak of holding back, and it wrings the heart.

s0063.literal: My course is decided. Please report this for me.
s0063.idiomatic: My mind is made up. Please lay this out on my behalf.

s0064.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys by hidden routes to Jiangling to report and receive the army's schedule and orders.
s0064.idiomatic: He then sent envoys by secret paths to Jiangling to report his arrival and receive the army's schedule and orders.

s0065.literal: At that time Cai Lubao had raised troops and held Nankang. Bo sent his trusted follower Tan Shiyuan as Magistrate of Qujiang to ally with Lubao and together block the righteous army.
s0065.idiomatic: At that time Cai Lubao had risen and seized Nankang. Bo sent his intimate Tan Shiyuan as magistrate of Qujiang to join with Lubao and together bar the loyal army's path.

s0066.literal: In the first month of the first year of Dabao the Founder set out from Shixing and halted at Dayu Ridge.
s0066.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Dabao the Founder marched from Shixing and camped at Dayu Ridge.

s0067.literal: Lubao sent out troops to encamp at Nanye, relying on mountains and rivers to build four walled camps to resist the Founder.
s0067.idiomatic: Lubao marched out and encamped at Nanye, using the terrain to raise four walled camps against the Founder.

s0068.literal: The Founder fought him and inflicted a great defeat. Lubao escaped in flight. The Founder advanced and encamped at Nankang.
s0068.idiomatic: The Founder gave battle and routed him utterly. Lubao fled for his life. The Founder pressed on and encamped at Nankang.

s0069.literal: Prince Xiangdong, acting on the regency commission, appointed the Founder Supernumerary Attendant Gentleman in Ordinary, Bearing the Staff, General of Illustrious Might, and Inspector of Jiaozhou, changing his enfeoffment to Baron of Nanye.
s0069.idiomatic: Prince Xiangdong, exercising regency powers, made the Founder supernumerary attendant gentleman in ordinary, bearer of the staff, general of illustrious might, and inspector of Jiaozhou, and changed his title to Baron of Nanye.

s0070.literal: In the sixth month the Founder repaired the old city at Qitou and moved his residence there.
s0070.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Founder restored the old fortress at Qitou and made it his seat.

s0071.literal: Li Qianshi, Inspector of Gaozhou, held Da Huang and sent his commander Du Pinglu with a thousand men into Ganshi and Yuliang. The Founder ordered Zhou Wenyü to lead troops, attack, and drive them off; Qianshi fled to Ningdu.
s0071.idiomatic: Li Qianshi, inspector of Gaozhou, held Da Huang and sent his commander Du Pinglu with a thousand men into Ganshi and Yuliang. The Founder sent Zhou Wenyü to strike and drive them off; Qianshi fled to Ningdu.

s0072.literal: Acting on the regency commission, he was appointed Unqualified Attendant Gentleman in Ordinary, Envoy Bearing the Staff, General of Trustworthy Might, and Inspector of Yuzhou, concurrently Interior Minister of Yuzhang, and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Changcheng.
s0072.idiomatic: By regency commission he was named unqualified attendant gentleman in ordinary, envoy bearing the staff, general of trustworthy might, and inspector of Yuzhou, with concurrent duties as interior minister of Yuzhang, and his title was raised to Marquis of Changcheng.

s0073.literal: Soon he was appointed Attendant Gentleman in Ordinary, Envoy Bearing the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs in six commanderies, General of the Army, and Inspector of South Jiangzhou, with the rest as before.
s0073.idiomatic: He was soon made attendant gentleman in ordinary, envoy bearing the staff, supervisor of military affairs in six commanderies, army general, and inspector of South Jiangzhou, with his other posts unchanged.

s0074.literal: At that time Liu Ai of Ningdu and others supplied Qianshi with boats, ships, and arms,[6] intending to raid Nankang. The Founder sent Du Sengming and others with twenty thousand men to hold Baikou and build a city for defense; Qianshi also built a city to confront them.
s0074.idiomatic: At that time Liu Ai of Ningdu and others furnished Qianshi with boats and weapons,[6] planning a strike at Nankang. The Founder sent Du Sengming and others with twenty thousand men to occupy Baikou and fortify it; Qianshi raised a facing camp as well.

s0075.literal: In the third month of the second year Sengming and the others stormed and took his city, captured Qianshi alive, and sent him to Nankang. The Founder executed him.
s0075.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year Sengming and his fellows stormed and took the city, seized Qianshi alive, and sent him to Nankang, where the Founder put him to death.

s0076.literal: The regency commission ordered the Founder to advance and pacify Jiangzhou, and he was further appointed Inspector of Jiangzhou, with the rest as before.
s0076.idiomatic: The regency commission ordered him to advance and settle Jiangzhou and further appointed him inspector of Jiangzhou, with his other posts unchanged.

s0077.literal: In the sixth month the Founder set out from Nankang.
s0077.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Founder marched from Nankang.

s0078.literal: At Ganshi in Nankang there were formerly twenty-four rapids, with many boulders in the shallows, which travelers regarded as difficult.
s0078.idiomatic: At Ganshi in Nankang there had long been twenty-four rapids strewn with boulders that travelers dreaded.

s0079.literal: When the Founder set out, the water rose several zhang in a sudden flood, and within three hundred li all the great stones were submerged.
s0079.idiomatic: When the Founder set out, the waters surged several zhang in a sudden flood, and for three hundred li every great stone lay drowned.

s0080.literal: Advancing, the army halted at Xichang. A dragon appeared at the water's edge, about five zhang in height, in the five colors, fresh and dazzling; tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians came to see it.
s0080.idiomatic: The army marched on and camped at Xichang. A dragon appeared at the riverbank, some five zhang tall, blazing in the five colors; tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians gathered to behold it.

s0081.literal: At that time the regency commission sent the General Who Conquers the East Wang Sengbian to supervise the army in attacking Hou Jing.
s0081.idiomatic: At that time the regency commission dispatched Wang Sengbian, general who conquers the east, to command the army against Hou Jing.

s0082.literal: In the eighth month Sengbian's army halted at Pen City.[7] The Founder led Du Sengming and others with the army and the magnates of the southern rivers, thirty thousand men in all, intending to join him there.
s0082.idiomatic: In the eighth month Sengbian's army camped at Pen City.[7] The Founder led Du Sengming and others with the army and the southern river lords—thirty thousand men in all—to rendezvous with him.

s0083.literal: At that time the western army lacked food. The Founder had earlier stored five hundred thousand piculs of grain for the army; now he divided three hundred thousand to supply them.
s0083.idiomatic: The western army was short of grain. The Founder had earlier laid up five hundred thousand piculs of army grain; now he gave them three hundred thousand.

s0085.literal: At that time Hou Jing had deposed Emperor Jianwen and enthroned the heir of Yuzhang, Prince Dong. The Founder sent his acting Chief Clerk Shen San to present a memorial at Jiangling urging advance to the throne.
s0085.idiomatic: Hou Jing had by then deposed Emperor Jianwen and set up Prince Dong, heir of Yuzhang. The Founder sent his acting chief clerk Shen San to Jiangling with a memorial urging the prince to take the throne.

s0086.literal: In the eleventh month the regency commission appointed the Founder Envoy Bearing the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs in the five commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of East Yangzhou, concurrently Administrator of Kuaiji and Interior Minister of Yuzhang, with the rest as before.
s0086.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the regency commission made him envoy bearing the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, general who pacifies the east, and inspector of East Yangzhou, with concurrent posts as administrator of Kuaiji and interior minister of Yuzhang, his other offices unchanged.

s0087.literal: In the first month of the third year the Founder led thirty thousand armored soldiers, five thousand strong crossbows, and two thousand boats, setting out from Yuzhang.
s0087.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year the Founder marched with thirty thousand armored men, five thousand heavy crossbows, and two thousand vessels from Yuzhang.

s0088.literal: In the second month he halted at Sangluo Isle and sent the Middle Recorder-Attendant Staff Officer Jiang Yuanli with a memorial of affairs to Jiangling; the regency commission added one set of imperial pipes and drums for the Founder.
s0088.idiomatic: In the second month he camped at Sangluo Isle and sent his middle recorder-attendant Jiang Yuanli to Jiangling with a report on affairs; the regency commission granted the Founder an additional set of imperial pipes and drums.

s0089.literal: At that time Sengbian had already set out from Pen City and met the Founder at Baimao Bay. They went ashore, built an altar, and sacrificed victims in covenant.
s0089.idiomatic: Sengbian had already left Pen City and met the Founder at Baimao Bay. They went ashore, raised an altar, and sealed their alliance with the blood of victims.

s0090.literal: Advancing, the army next halted at Wuhu. Zhang He, Hou Jing's garrison commander, abandoned the city and fled.
s0090.idiomatic: The army pressed on to Wuhu. Zhang He, Hou Jing's garrison commander there, abandoned the city and fled.

s0091.literal: In the third month the Founder advanced with the armies and stormed Gushu,[8] then next halted at Cai Isle.
s0091.idiomatic: In the third month the Founder advanced with the allied armies and took Gushu,[8] then camped at Cai Isle.

s0092.literal: Hou Jing ascended Stone City to observe the situation and was greatly displeased. He told those at his side: "Above this army there is purple vapor; they will not be easy to withstand.
s0092.idiomatic: Hou Jing climbed Stone City to survey the field and was deeply unsettled. He told his attendants, "Purple qi hangs over this army; they will not be easy to face.

s0093.literal: " He had rafts loaded with stones sunk to block the mouth of the Huai, and along the Huai built a wall from Stone City to Qingxi for more than ten li, with watchtowers and battlements linked together.
s0093.idiomatic: " He sank rafts laden with stone to choke the Huai mouth and built a wall along the river from Stone City to Qingxi for more than ten li, watchtowers and parapets linked end to end.

s0094.literal: The generals had not yet decided. Sengbian sent Du Kan to ask the Founder's plan. The Founder said: "Earlier Liu Zhongli with several hundred thousand men sat across the water, and Wei Can at Qingxi in the end did not cross to the north bank. The bandits climbed high to look on, saw through us inside and out, and indulged their cruelty, overturning our royal army.
s0094.idiomatic: The commanders could not agree. Sengbian sent Du Kan to ask the Founder's counsel. The Founder said, "Before this, Liu Zhongli sat with hundreds of thousands across the water, and Wei Can at Qingxi never crossed to the north bank. The rebels looked down from the heights, saw everything inside and out, and ran riot, destroying our imperial host.

s0095.literal: Now besieging Stone City, we must cross to the north bank.
s0095.idiomatic: Now, besieging Stone City, we must cross to the north bank.

s0096.literal: If the generals cannot meet the enemy's edge, let them go first and build stockades.
s0096.idiomatic: If any commander cannot meet the enemy head-on, let him go first and build stockades.

s0097.literal: " The Founder immediately built stockades on the transverse ridge west of Stone City. The army encamped in succession at eight walled positions, thrusting straight out to the northeast.
s0097.idiomatic: " The Founder at once threw up stockades on the ridge west of Stone City. The army camped in a chain of eight fortified positions, driving straight toward the northeast.

s0098.literal: Fearing that the road to West Province would be cut, the bandits also built five walled positions in the Guolin of the northeast to block the great road.
s0098.idiomatic: Fearing their line to West Province would be severed, the rebels likewise raised five walled camps in the northeast orchards to choke the main road.

s0099.literal: Jing led more than ten thousand men and over eight hundred iron cavalry, forming battle lines as he advanced.
s0099.idiomatic: Hou Jing led more than ten thousand men and over eight hundred armored horsemen, advancing in battle formation.

s0100.literal: The Founder said: "The military chronicles have it that one who uses troops well is like the snake of Mount Chang—head and tail respond to each other.
s0100.idiomatic: The Founder said, "The manuals of war say that the master of arms is like the serpent of Mount Chang: strike the head and the tail answers; strike the tail and the head answers.
